note: One entry per stock for its page on the desk: sector, valuation (with its source and date), the latest session's trading, dates coming up and news. The daily run updates it; news is kept, newest first, and never deleted.

valuation.basis: results for the 12 months to September 2026

next.why: The October 29 hike of 100 basis points widened lending margins; another move would matter as much.

news.text: Chief executive Hisham Ezz Al Arab said third-quarter operating profit rose about 18% excluding one-offs in last year's quarter, and expected-loss adjustments went to a special reserve.

Nine-month consolidated profit rose 1.6% to EGP 63.1bn; third-quarter profit fell 17.4% to EGP 23.8bn against a 2025 quarter with an EGP 13.1bn provision release. Margin 8.02% in the quarter; deposits EGP 1.45tn (Mubasher Banks, Fintechgate).
Deputy chief executive Amr El-Ganainy said its Yomo digital bank has the central bank's preliminary approval and is completing the requirements for a final license (Banky, Tawasol).
Raised its monthly floating-rate certificate to 20.50% from 19.50% and its daily one to 20.25% after the central bank's 100 bps hike; the floors are 17.50% and 17.25%.
CIB led listed banks on Monday, rising 2.9% to EGP 121.40, while ADIB Egypt fell 3.4% and Crédit Agricole Egypt 3.0%; an asset manager said funds are concentrating in the most liquid name.
CIB rose 0.5% to EGP 120.47 on the day the central bank raised rates by 100 basis points.
Commercial International Bank closed at its lowest since 31 March as the EGX30 fell 1.6%.

filed.how: 63,080,000,000 this year to date + 82,238,000,000 last year - 62,100,000,000 a year earlier

lastResults.headline: Nine-month profit up 1.6% to EGP 63.1bn; third quarter down 17.4% to EGP 23.8bn against a quarter flattered by a one-off provision release
points: No published consensus: against last year, nine-month consolidated profit rose to EGP 63.1bn from EGP 62.1bn; the bank puts underlying growth at 18% (9% in dollars).
Net interest income rose 18.6% to EGP 93.3bn; the net interest margin was 8.02% in the quarter against 8.40% for the nine months, reflecting cuts through February.
Deposits rose 30.5% this year to about EGP 1.45tn and assets 26.6% to EGP 1.83tn; bad loans 1.47%, covered 343%; capital adequacy 28.8%.
Management targets EGP 80–85bn for 2026, leaving about EGP 17–22bn for the fourth quarter (Al Ahly Pharos via Al Mal).
lastResults.thesis: No change to the desk's margin view: the October 29 hike lifts margins only from the fourth quarter, and at about 4.8 times earnings the results risk has passed.

brief.business: Egypt's largest private bank and the EGX30's heaviest stock. It earns the gap between what it pays depositors and what loans and government bills pay it: net interest income was EGP 93.3bn in nine months, against profit of EGP 63.1bn.

drivers.name: Interest rates
drivers.text: The margin was 8.02% in the third quarter, down from 8.40% for the nine months as earlier cuts fed through; October's 100-point hike works the other way.

drivers.name: Deposit growth
drivers.text: Deposits rose 30.5% this year to about EGP 1.45tn. More cheap deposits put into bills at 26% is the simplest source of profit.

drivers.name: Bad loans
drivers.text: 1.47% of loans, covered 343%, with capital adequacy at 28.8%: there is room to absorb a weak year.

drivers.name: Foreign money
drivers.text: The most liquid Egyptian stock, so it rises first when foreigners return and falls first when they leave.

brief.value: 4.9 times earnings and 1.6 times book for a 34% return on equity. The desk's fair value is about EGP 159, measured against other banks only.
risks: Rate cuts arriving faster than loan growth can make up.
A tax or reserve change on banks' bill holdings.
Last year's profit included an EGP 13.1bn provision release, so reported growth looks weak until the fourth quarter laps it.
brief.change: Management targets EGP 80–85bn of profit for 2026. A fourth quarter under about EGP 17bn would miss it and weaken the case.

news.text: Signed an agreement with the state to develop four mixed-use projects in East Cairo, Alexandria and the North Coast, with targeted investment of about EGP 11 trillion over more than 37 million square metres. President El-Sisi also asked the government to work with the group on 200,000 homes for rent.

valuation.basis: results for the 12 months to June 2026

brief.business: Talaat Moustafa is Egypt's largest developer by sales (Madinaty, Noor, the North Coast) and owns hotels that earn in dollars. It signed a deal with the state on October 28 to develop four projects with targeted investment of about EGP 11 trillion.

drivers.name: Sales and the land bank
drivers.text: Scale lets it sell on long instalment plans others cannot match.

drivers.name: Hotels
drivers.text: A recurring dollar income that developers without hotels lack.

drivers.name: Interest rates
drivers.text: As for every developer, dear money slows buyers; the desk's open view has developers lagging while rates stay high.

brief.value: 11.5 times earnings and 1.9 times book. Analysts' targets are well above the price on the land bank; today's earnings and book value put it slightly below. The desk's fair value is about EGP 80.
risks: Execution on a deal far larger than anything it has built.
Rates staying high.
A richer valuation than other developers leaves less margin.
brief.change: Detail on how the state deal is financed and when it starts to earn.

news.text: Signed a EGP 76.17m contract with the Arab Organization for Industrialization for 3 MW of solar plants at its Alexandria site, due within 12 months.

Notified that its gas supply cut rises to 33% from 20% from November 8; two of its three plants run at full capacity and maintenance has been rescheduled (Mubasher, Reuters). The stock fell 5.8% to EGP 76.30.
Filed nine-month net profit of EGP 12.97bn, up 102.8%, on revenue of EGP 31.49bn, up 89.9%, on 29 October (one outlet; the stock rose 3.0% to EGP 80.00).

CI Capital expects lower gas allocations to weigh on Abu Qir, Mopco and Valmore's Alexfert in the fourth quarter and possibly through 2027; granular urea is fetching about $535 a ton FOB, up 17% since September.

Told the EGX it reduced its natural gas intake from 1 November after receiving a supply-cut notice, without giving the percentage; production continues under contingency plans for inventory and rescheduled maintenance. Kima and Mopco each reported a 20% cut. The stock fell 3.6% to EGP 77.71.
Unaudited nine-month profit rose to about EGP 12.97bn, roughly double a year earlier, helped by steadier gas supplies.

The board awarded the second phase of its solar plants, about 3 MW for EGP 76.2m over 12 months, to the Arab Organization for Industrialization, and approved a McKinsey-drafted strategy to start in fiscal 2027.

valuation.source: Company filing (Arab Finance (unaudited statement filed to the EGX 29 Oct); Al Borsa)

brief.business: Abu Qir Fertilizers makes urea and nitrates at three plants in Alexandria for the local market and for export. Nine-month profit doubled to EGP 12.97bn on revenue of EGP 31.49bn.

drivers.name: Gas supply
drivers.text: Its cut rose to 33% from 20% on November 8; two of three plants are running at full capacity and maintenance has been rescheduled.

drivers.name: Urea prices
drivers.text: Granular urea is about $535 a ton, up 17% since September, which softens the lost volume.

drivers.name: The dividend
drivers.text: A yield above 11%, paid from those earnings.

brief.value: 7.7 times earnings with the three estimates close together, near EGP 93. CI Capital expects lower gas allocations to weigh on the fourth quarter and possibly through 2027.
risks: The gas cut deepening or lasting through 2027.
A fall in urea prices.
A firmer pound lowering export income in pounds.
brief.change: Gas allocations restored, or fourth-quarter volumes showing how much the cut costs.

lastResults.headline: Nine-month profit up 103% to EGP 12.97bn on revenue up 90% to EGP 31.49bn
points: No published consensus: net profit after tax rose to EGP 12.97bn from EGP 6.40bn, standalone and unaudited; revenue EGP 31.49bn against EGP 16.58bn.
The company credits steady gas supply, volumes up 22% and export volumes up 55%, all before the November gas cuts.
lastResults.thesis: Strong, but backward-looking: the gas cut to 33% since November 8 will show in the fourth quarter, so the desk's bearish gas view stands.

brief.business: Palm Hills builds and sells homes in west and east Cairo and on the North Coast, mostly on instalments over several years. Profit is booked when homes are delivered, so it trails sales by years.

drivers.name: Interest rates
drivers.text: Buyers pay in instalments and the company borrows to build; dearer money hurts both. The desk has an open view that developers lag while rates stay high.

drivers.name: Sales and deliveries
drivers.text: New sales show demand today; deliveries decide reported profit.

drivers.name: Land
drivers.text: Al Ahly Pharos values it at EGP 21.40 a share on existing assets alone.

brief.value: 7.2 times earnings and 1.8 times book. The desk's fair value is about EGP 16.50, with all three estimates above the price.
risks: Rates staying high through 2027.
Cancellations if buyers' incomes lag instalments.
Construction costs rising faster than contracted prices.
brief.change: Results on November 16: sales holding up at these rates would favor the cheap valuation over the desk's shorter-term caution.

watch: New sales: the EGP 75bn booked at Hacienda Ras El-Hekma in its first two weeks counts in the third quarter, the test of demand at 25% bill yields.
Gross margin, after first-half EBITDA margin fell to 21% from 29%.
Profit attributable, after the first half fell 7% to EGP 2.26bn on revenue up 25.4%.
Backlog against the record EGP 284bn at the end of June, and cancellations.

news.text: Signed a non-binding agreement with Venezuela and PDVSA on November 9 to assess seven oil and gas areas, with a year's exclusive talks.
Chief executive Darren Woods pulled out of COP31 in Antalya, citing security logistics; he was the only major oil chief due to speak.
Signed a preliminary agreement with PDVSA to assess producing and new fields in Venezuela, with reserves in the billions of barrels; no investment figure (Reuters, teleSUR).
Third-quarter profit roughly doubled to $15.4bn from $7.5bn a year earlier, on revenue up about 33% to $113.2bn, beating estimates on higher oil prices and record output.

news.text: Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services were disrupted from Thursday into Friday; Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack.
Fell 2.3% to $521.13 after Anthropic launched Claude Sheets and other office tools; a filing showed the chief financial officer sold about 7,305 shares.
Lobbied the administration to drop proposed curbs on Chinese optical transceivers, warning they could leave AI chips idle in data centers.
Fell 2.2% to $533.16 after Anthropic unveiled workplace tools including Claude Sheets, a spreadsheet rival to Excel.
Is ending a 2023 deal to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle, which runs on older Nvidia chips, Bloomberg reported; Microsoft fell 1.0% to $530.61.

Microsoft reportedly declined an option that would have more than doubled its Texas compute agreement with Nscale; Reuters could not verify the Financial Times report. The stock rose 6.7% to a record $555.80.
Lined up a $25bn bond sale to fund AI spending, its first bond sale since 2017.

news.text: Rose 3.2% to $288.93 after the midterm result; data-centre regulation was a campaign issue and analysts argue it favours large operators.
Raised EUR 6bn in a bond sale with about EUR 17bn of orders, covered 2.8 times against nearly five times in February.
UBS cut its price target to $332 from $380 and kept a neutral rating after search and YouTube revenue missed forecasts.

news.text: Fell 4.8% to $347.01 on Friday, giving back Thursday's gain as the Philadelphia semiconductor index lost 3.4%.
Rothschild Redburn cut it to neutral from buy with a $398 target, from $595, citing the durability of AI earnings; the stock rose 5.5% to $364.36 on Thursday.
Rose 3.9% to $331.98 after Anthropic's amended filing named it a roughly $1.0bn buyer in a $26bn private placement at the IPO price.
A $63bn financing deal tied to Anthropic gives Broadcom a funded customer for its AI chip forecast, according to 24/7 Wall St.; reported by one outlet so far.

news.text: Nine-month profit rose 44% to EGP 24.4bn on revenue up 19% to EGP 93.6bn; EBITDA rose 24% to EGP 43.1bn, a 46% margin, and net debt fell to 0.8 times EBITDA. Mubasher's 88% rise compares with a lower prior-year figure than the company's own.
MSCI adds it to the MSCI Egypt standard index at the close on November 30, replacing Eastern Company.
The Suez Canal Economic Zone hired Telecom Egypt to upgrade networks across its ports and industrial zones, including East Port Said and Sokhna (EnterpriseAM, Zawya).
Chief executive Tamer El-Mahdy said Telecom Egypt targets about $500m of network investment over five years and that subsea cable revenue grew 31% last fiscal year.
Signed a strategic agreement with the Suez Canal Economic Zone to build telecom networks and digital services across its industrial zones and ports; no value was disclosed.
The board approved a 2027 budget guiding low double-digit revenue growth and an EBITDA margin in the low-to-mid 40s.

watch: Revenue growth against the 2027 budget's low double-digit guidance, and how much of it is pricing after the currency slide.
EBITDA margin against the guided low-to-mid forties, with power and dollar costs up.
Capex and dollar debt: the stock has doubled this year (+103.7%) on cash flow, so free cash flow matters as much as profit.
Vodafone Egypt's dividend and income from its 45% stake, a large part of net profit.
Wholesale and international cable revenue, the dollar earner, as Red Sea traffic returns.

brief.business: Telecom Egypt owns the country's fixed-line network and sells broadband, wholesale capacity to the mobile operators and transit on the subsea cables that land in Egypt; it also holds a large stake in Vodafone Egypt. Subsea cable revenue grew 31% last fiscal year.

drivers.name: Data demand
drivers.text: Broadband and wholesale data grow with usage and with each price rise the regulator allows.

drivers.name: Subsea cables
drivers.text: Dollar income from carriers that cross Egypt between Europe and Asia, the line growing fastest.

drivers.name: Investment and debt
drivers.text: It plans about $500m of network spending over five years; its 2027 budget guides low double-digit revenue growth and an EBITDA margin in the low-to-mid 40s.

brief.value: 11.3 times last year's consolidated earnings and 3.1 times book. The three estimates agree, and put fair value near EGP 123, about 9% below the price after a year in which the stock roughly doubled.
risks: A run of 105% this year leaves little room for a miss.
Dollar debt and capital spending if the pound weakens.
Regulated prices and spectrum fees.
brief.change: Results on November 12: margin against the budget's low-to-mid 40s range.

filed.how: 24,390,000,000 this year to date + 22,554,000,000 last year - 16,968,000,000 a year earlier
filed.source: Telecom Egypt 9M 2026 release; Arab Finance for 2025 and 9M 2025

lastResults.headline: Against last year (no published estimate): nine-month profit up 44% to EGP 24.4bn on revenue up 19%
points: Revenue EGP 93.6bn, up 19%, led by data (+30%) and international incoming calls (+25%, with traffic up 16% and a weaker pound).
EBITDA EGP 43.1bn, up 24%, a 46% margin against 44% a year earlier; net margin 26%.
Net debt 0.8 times annualized EBITDA, from 1.5 times; free cash flow EGP 28.0bn and cash capex EGP 26.3bn.
Outlets' 88% rise (Mubasher) rests on a lower prior-year figure than the company's 44%.
lastResults.thesis: Earnings grew faster than revenue and debt fell, and MSCI's inclusion on November 30 adds index buying; the desk opens a low-confidence view that the stock holds above EGP 122.

news.text: Nine-month consolidated profit rose 16% to EGP 16.4bn from EGP 14.1bn on revenue of EGP 263bn, up from EGP 199.7bn; standalone profit fell to EGP 4.27bn.
Launched RYZE elevators, escalators and walkways with EGP 100m of initial investment and a target of EGP 1bn of sales in 2027; the group targets $7bn of revenue this year.

brief.business: Elsewedy Electric makes cables, transformers and meters and builds power and infrastructure projects across Africa and the Gulf. It targets $7bn of revenue this year, much of it earned in hard currency.

drivers.name: The order book abroad
drivers.text: Turnkey projects and cable exports are where growth comes from, and they are paid in dollars.

drivers.name: The pound
drivers.text: A weaker pound flatters its earnings in pounds; the pound's rise to 53.39 does the opposite.

drivers.name: Copper and aluminium
drivers.text: Its main inputs; prices pass through to customers with a lag.

brief.value: 16 times earnings against about 11 for industrials, and 3.7 times book. All three of the desk's estimates sit below the price; fair value is about EGP 95.
risks: A firmer pound cutting translated profit.
A slow quarter for project awards.
Paying a full price leaves no room for a miss.
brief.change: Results on November 16. Profit growth well above the 6% of the past year would justify the premium; another flat quarter would not.

lastResults.headline: Against last year (no published estimate): nine-month profit up 16% to EGP 16.4bn on revenue up 32%
points: Consolidated revenue EGP 263bn against EGP 199.7bn a year earlier (Mubasher, Alborsa).
Consolidated profit EGP 16.4bn against EGP 14.1bn, so margins narrowed as revenue grew twice as fast as profit.
Standalone profit fell to EGP 4.27bn from EGP 5.73bn.
A consortium including Elsewedy won a $2.2bn EPC contract for Saudi Arabia's Rabigh 2 plant (Alborsa).
lastResults.thesis: Growth of 16% sits below what a stock up 55% this year prices, which keeps it on the dear side of the desk's value basket.

news.text: The 900 MW Gulf of Suez III wind farm, 25% owned by Orascom with ENGIE and Aeolus, reached financial close; Orascom does the civil and electrical works, and full operation is due in September 2028.

The board allotted 97.2 million new $1 shares to OCI N.V., raising capital to $207.4m from $110.2m; the shares are due to list on the EGX and ADX on November 24, with completion in December (Arab Finance).
The board meets on 5 November to approve a capital increase to $207.4m from $110.2m, the step behind the OCI merger; the stock rose 0.9% to EGP 797.02.
The board is due on 5 November to approve a capital increase to $207.4m from $110.2m through 97.2m new shares for OCI N.V., the step behind their merger, per an EGX disclosure.
Expects to complete the OCI merger in December; the board meets on Thursday to approve a capital increase and allot 97.2 million new shares, with listing targeted for 24 November.
OCI N.V. shareholders approved the Orascom Construction combination; Amsterdam delisting is set for November (headline-level, TradingView and TipRanks).

next.event: New OCI shares list on the EGX and ADX (target)
next.why: 97.2 million new shares; crediting to OCI holders from about December 8.

brief.business: Orascom Construction builds infrastructure, industrial and commercial projects in Egypt, the Gulf and the United States, and is merging with OCI N.V. The board has allotted 97.2 million new shares to OCI, raising capital to $207.4m from $110.2m.

drivers.name: The merger
drivers.text: OCI brings assets valued at $1.35bn against Orascom's $1.52bn; existing holders keep about 53% of the combined company. Completion is expected in December.

drivers.name: The backlog
drivers.text: New awards in Egypt and the Gulf decide revenue two to three years out.

drivers.name: The pound
drivers.text: Much of its work is paid in dollars, so a weaker pound flatters results in pounds.

brief.value: Not rated by the desk for now: every per-share figure predates the new shares, so a P/E of 7.9 on old earnings says little about the merged company.
risks: What OCI's assets earn once inside the group.
Execution on large state projects and their payment terms.
New shares arriving on the market from November 24.
brief.change: The first accounts of the merged company, and how the new shares trade after they list on November 24.

news.text: A group linked to an insider bought 100,000 shares in Sunday's session (Youm7).

brief.business: Fawry runs Egypt's largest bill-payment network and has built lending, merchant acquiring and banking services on top of it. First-half revenue was EGP 5.2bn and profit for shareholders EGP 1.6bn.

drivers.name: Lending
drivers.text: Consumer and small-business credit is the fastest-growing line and the most sensitive to rates and bad debts.

drivers.name: Payment volumes
drivers.text: Rise with inflation and with the shift from cash.

drivers.name: Regulation
drivers.text: Fees and licenses are set by the central bank and the FRA.

brief.value: The estimates disagree more than for any other desk stock: 19 times earnings is dear against its peers, while Al Ahly Pharos puts fair value at EGP 28.60 on its growth. The desk's figure, near the price, is low confidence.
risks: Credit losses rising in the lending book.
A cap on payment fees.
Competition from banks' own apps and InstaPay.
brief.change: Two more quarters of profit growth above 40% would settle the argument in the brokers' favor.

news.text: EFG Hermes was joint offering manager of DIB Holding's AED 1.94bn ($529m) IPO on the Dubai Financial Market, priced at AED 1.12 a share.

EFG Hermes ended its advisory role in the Banque du Caire offering, saying orders topped $4.6bn; the stock fell 3.4% to EGP 22.36, a 52-week low, and the group says more IPOs are lined up before year-end and early 2027.
EFG Hermes launched Younit, Egypt's first platform offering retail investors algorithmic trading through APIs.
EFG Hermes is among ten brokers preparing to launch short selling on the EGX in November, per Shorouk (sources; no exact date).
Banque du Caire's retail tranche closed about 27 times covered; trading is expected on Monday 2 November.

brief.business: EFG Holding is the region's largest investment bank (EFG Hermes: brokerage, advisory, asset management) with a commercial bank and non-bank finance arms. It was joint offering manager of DIB Holding's AED 1.94bn IPO in Dubai and advised on Banque du Caire's.

drivers.name: Market turnover
drivers.text: Brokerage fees follow trading: the EGX's turnover on November 10 was the highest in a year.

drivers.name: Deal flow
drivers.text: Listings in Egypt and the Gulf; the group says more are lined up before year-end and early 2027.

drivers.name: The lending businesses
drivers.text: Steadier income, sensitive to rates and bad debts.

brief.value: 8.9 times earnings and priced at its book value, with a return on equity of 11%. The three estimates agree near EGP 29.50.
risks: A quiet market after the IPO wave.
Credit losses in consumer and small-business lending.
Earnings spread across currencies, so results swing with the pound.
brief.change: Results on November 18: whether the busiest turnover in a year shows up in brokerage income.

brief.business: Cleopatra Hospitals runs a group of private hospitals in Cairo. It earns from occupancy and from the prices insurers and patients pay.

drivers.name: Volumes
drivers.text: Beds filled and operations performed.

drivers.name: Price increases
drivers.text: Private healthcare prices have risen with inflation, 12.7% in October.

drivers.name: New capacity
drivers.text: Each hospital added lifts revenue before it lifts profit.

brief.value: 32 times last year's earnings, a growth multiple. The desk's model allows growth only 25%, so it puts fair value near EGP 12.70, below the price, while analysts' targets sit close to it.

Staff and drug costs rising faster than prices.
Few recent figures on the desk: the note rests mainly on valuation.

Margins: costs at new hospitals and staff pay against price rises, with October inflation at 12.7%.
Revenue growth against the first half's 27.4%, as the base for a stock at about 32 times last year's earnings.
Finance costs at 20%-plus rates on any borrowing for expansion.

news.text: On its call: third-quarter revenue up 25% to EGP 10bn, net profit up 33% to EGP 654m after a EGP 107m currency loss; the fourth quarter is guided at the same pace. The stock fell 2.3% to EGP 24.13.
Nine-month consolidated profit rose 60% to EGP 2.04bn from EGP 1.27bn on sales up 25% to EGP 27.66bn; standalone profit rose 47% to EGP 1.41bn.
Took a six-year, $36m facility from CIB ($31.6m and EGP 255m) to build a citrus production line for its concentrate exports, disclosed to the exchange.

Raises prices from November 8: Bekhayro laban 1 kg to EGP 44 from EGP 42.5, Mix 200 ml to EGP 15 from EGP 13.5 and Juhayna laban 200 ml to EGP 15 from EGP 14, citing production costs (Masrawy, Al Khabar Live).

watch: Volumes after price rises of 4–11% on key dairy lines in early November and earlier in the year.
Gross margin with poultry feed, oils and packaging costs up; urban food inflation is still rising month on month.
Growth against the first half's 23% rise in attributable profit to EGP 1.38bn.
Export and concentrate sales, the dollar earner behind the new $36m citrus line.

lastResults.headline: Against last year (no published estimate): nine-month profit up 60% to EGP 2.04bn on sales up 25%
points: Consolidated net profit EGP 2.04bn against EGP 1.27bn a year earlier; first-half profit attributable was EGP 1.38bn, so the third quarter added about EGP 0.65bn.
Net sales rose 25% to EGP 27.66bn from EGP 22.13bn, ahead of 2025's full-year growth of about 23%.
Standalone profit rose 47% to EGP 1.41bn; the subsidiary Inmaa took an EGP 1.73bn CIB loan for livestock.

brief.business: Juhayna is Egypt's largest dairy and juice maker. Nine-month profit rose 60% to EGP 2.04bn on sales up 25% to EGP 27.66bn.

drivers.name: Prices against costs
drivers.text: It raised prices again on November 8 (Bekhayro milk to EGP 44 a kilogram from 42.5), citing production costs.

drivers.name: Volumes
drivers.text: Whether shoppers keep buying after repeated increases.

drivers.name: Expansion
drivers.text: A $36m CIB facility for a citrus line for concentrate exports, and an EGP 1.73bn loan for its livestock arm.

brief.value: 16.4 times earnings against about 12 for consumer stocks. The desk's projection (EGP 27–28 by end of January) rests on results momentum; its fair value, near EGP 19.40, says the price already holds a lot of it.
risks: Price rises meeting resistance as inflation slows.
Raw milk and feed costs.
New borrowing at today's rates.
brief.change: Fourth-quarter sales volumes after the November price rise.

news.text: Al Ahly Pharos sees no buying opportunity at current prices despite first-half net profit of about EGP 3.8bn and net cash of EGP 5.5bn.
Naeem kept its EGP 33.6 target after nine-month results, citing container volumes and wider margins; the stock closed at EGP 33.00.
Nine-month net profit rose 16% to EGP 5.725bn from EGP 4.951bn, on revenue up 7% to EGP 6.772bn; the figures are unaudited.

brief.business: Alexandria Containers runs container terminals at Alexandria and Dekheila ports and is paid mostly in dollars. Nine-month profit rose 16% to EGP 5.73bn on revenue up 7% to EGP 6.77bn.

drivers.name: Container volumes
drivers.text: Follow Egypt's trade; Suez traffic is running 36% above last year.

drivers.name: The pound
